# `Q-20-6` — Callout Has No Registered Crossref Category

> A callout's identifier prefix is a recognized cross-reference type, but
> not one registered for callout/figure-style numbering.

## What this means

A callout's identifier (e.g. `#thm-x`) starts with a prefix Quarto
recognizes as a cross-reference type in general, but that prefix is not one
of the categories registered for callout/figure-style numbering
specifically. Quarto 1 would abort the whole render in this situation; the
pandoc-leg shim instead renders the callout without a number, so the
document still builds. Any `@ref` to that callout will not resolve to a
number, since none was assigned.

## Why this happens

- The identifier prefix belongs to another cross-reference family (for
  example a theorem-environment prefix like `thm-`, `lem-`, `cor-`) that
  was used on a callout by mistake.
- A custom or extension-registered cross-reference prefix was applied to a
  callout without also registering it for callout-style numbering.

## How to fix

Give the callout an identifier prefix that is registered for numbering
(for example `note-`, `tip-`, `warning-`, `important-`, `caution-`), or
remove the numeric-looking prefix entirely if the callout was never meant
to be numbered.

## Related errors

- [`Q-20-5`](Q-20-5.qmd) — a different pandoc-leg fallback, for an entirely
  unrecognized custom node type rather than a callout with an
  unregistered crossref category.
